claims.text: The study identified 249 intravenous drug errors.
At least one error occurred in 212 of 430 intravenous drug doses (49%, 95% confidence interval 45% to 54%).
claims.note: Span [6] matches exactly, including 212/430 and 49% (45% to 54%).

claims.text: Three doses (1%) had potentially severe errors, 126 (29%) potentially moderate errors, and 83 (19%) potentially minor errors.
claims.note: Span [7] matches the counts and percentages exactly.

claims.text: Most errors occurred when giving bolus doses or making up drugs that required multiple step preparation.
The authors concluded that the rate of intravenous drug errors was high.
claims.note: Span [9] CONCLUSIONS states the rate of intravenous drug errors was high.

claims.text: The authors suggested that reducing ward preparation, training, and technology for slow bolus administration would likely have the greatest effect on error rates.
claims.note: Span [11] conveys the same combination of reducing ward preparation, training, and technology for slow bolus doses.
